headline: An App Store ranking moved a trillion dollars
standfirst: Meta's Muse agent took the top of the US iPhone free chart and the semiconductor complex repriced around it: Meta rose 11.43%, AMD 9.95% to close above a $1 trillion market capitalisation for the first time, Intel 12% and Arm 17%. The Nasdaq Composite closed at 27,122.09, a record and its first since 2 June, the S&P 500 at 7,764.70 and the Dow at 52,048.83. Underneath it, crude fell to an eleven-day low on Strait of Hormuz shipping data and the ten-year came back under 5% at 4.96%. Treasury sells $69 billion of two-years at 13:00 ET into that, with Williams, Jefferson and Barkin all speaking first.

bullets.title: One product ranking, four chipmakers, a trillion dollars
bullets.text: Muse, Meta's personal AI agent, launched two weeks ago and has now been the most downloaded free iPhone app in the US for three days running, ahead of ChatGPT, on Sensor Tower's data — roughly 600,000 downloads in its first five days. The trade that followed is a CPU trade, not a GPU one: agents chain tool calls and orchestrate steps, which is general-purpose compute. AMD rose 9.95% to $615.52, a record close and its first $1 trillion valuation, making it the fourth US chip company there after Nvidia, Broadcom and Micron; Intel added 12%, Arm 17%, Qualcomm about 6%. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose 4.3%, its best day since 4 August and a fifth straight gain. Meta itself added about $194 billion of market value in a session, its strongest since April 2025, helped by a Wells Fargo target raised from $640 to $796.

bullets.title: The oil half of the day was a shipping report
bullets.text: US Central Command put oil and LNG movements through the Strait of Hormuz at their highest in six months over the past fortnight, and satellite tracking showed Saudi Aramco loading about 14 million barrels onto seven large tankers. WTI fell about 5% to $95.16 intraday, an eleven-day low, and Brent settled near $100.34 after dipping below $100. Energy was the only S&P sector down, at −2.88%, against technology's +2.77% and communication services' +3.56% — ten of eleven sectors rose. Crude has given back 8.26% over five sessions and is still up 62% year to date.

bullets.title: The ten-year fell back under five. The two-year did not move.
bullets.text: The benchmark ten-year closed at about 4.95%, down roughly 4bp, after touching 5.041% last week — a nineteen-year high. The thirty-year fell a similar amount to 5.286%. The two-year, the policy-sensitive end, closed at 4.751%, up slightly, having traded 4.772% intraday, its highest since July 2024. German and UK ten-years fell about 5bp alongside. That is a long-end rally on the oil print sitting on top of an unmoved front end: 2s10s is 20bp against 25bp on Friday, and futures still price roughly 88% odds of another Fed hike in December.

bullets.title: The supply the week is really about starts today
bullets.text: Treasury sells $69 billion of two-years at 13:00 ET, with the previous stop at 4.204% and the front end 50bp higher over the month. Five-years follow Wednesday, seven-years Thursday. New York Fed President Williams speaks at 10:05 ET, Vice Chair Jefferson at 10:20 and Richmond's Barkin at 13:00, the same minute the auction closes. With Warsh giving no forward guidance between meetings, the speeches are the only read on the path — and a soft two-year tail would say the market does not believe the dots it has just sold off for.

bullets.title: What the sell-side thinks breaks this
bullets.text: Morgan Stanley has said the S&P 500 could fall as much as 7% if energy prices rise further and the ten-year stays near 5%. On the other side, HSBC now sees the ten-year at 4.65% by year-end, iCapital at 5.3%, and Miller Tabak's Matt Maley argues a sustained break above 4.8% is the nearer-term test rather than any run at 6%. Forecasts cluster between 4.65% and 5.3%. This week's flash PMIs, Thursday's claims and the Fed speeches are what decides which camp is right.

calendar.note: Her second appearance in two days, a day before the euro-area flash PMIs. The ECB is at 2.50% and has said no meeting is ruled out, October included.
The weekly series, not the monthly print, which lands 30 September. Previous average 16,250. The only labour reading before Thursday's claims.
Seen at 5 after 4. Worth watching this week only as an early read on tomorrow's flash PMIs.
Williams runs the New York desk and Jefferson is Vice Chair. Between them they are the closest thing to guidance the Fed is giving right now.

calendar.event: $69bn two-year note auction; Fed's Barkin speaks
calendar.note: Previous stop 4.204%. The two-year is 4.76% and has moved 12% over the month. The tail is the number, not the yield.

calendar.event: US flash PMIs (September); euro area 04:00, UK 04:30
calendar.note: US manufacturing seen 53.5 after 53.9, services 56.0 after 56.5. UK manufacturing has been marked down to 51.4 from 52.7 since yesterday. A strong flash reads hawkish, not as good news.

calendar.event: Jobless claims; SNB decision 03:30; $44bn seven-year auction 13:00
calendar.note: Claims seen 203,000 after 196,000, revised up from 202,000 yesterday. The SNB is expected to hold at zero.
Durable goods seen −0.3% after +1.1%, ex-transport +0.6%, core capital goods +0.5% off a July now revised to flat. Michigan sentiment 47.5, one-year inflation expectations 4.6%.

sessionNote: Asia extended the move and the commodity and crypto tapes have partly given it back. The Kospi rose about 1.6% with SK Hynix up as much as 3.6% and Samsung 3.5%; the Korea ETF had already risen 4.33% on Monday and Taiwan 3.58%, though a third of the Korean move is the won, which gained 1.40% against the dollar. Overnight, WTI has bounced 1.21% to $93.49 and Brent 1.51% to $101.86, and Bitcoin, which traded above $86,000 during Monday's session, is back at $85,152, down 1.46%. So the two things that drove Monday — cheaper oil and risk appetite — are both slightly worse this morning than they were at the New York close.
watchOut: Treating an App Store ranking as a revenue line. Meta is up about 21% since Muse launched a fortnight ago and AMD is up roughly 183% this year and 30% this month, on a download chart and a distribution metric. AMD's own management describes the agentic share of its server-CPU market as a projection rather than a booked line, and the $220 billion figure it points at is a 2030 number. A broker target that moves from $640 to $796 in one note is describing sentiment, not earnings. Meanwhile the input that actually moved the whole board — crude — has already bounced overnight, and a ten-year at 4.96% is four basis points from being back where it was on Friday.

archive.headline: The war premium leaks out before the UN
archive.summary: Monday with no US data and a live diplomatic wire. Crude fell for a fourth session as traders priced a chance of US–Iran contact at the UN General Assembly and Saudi Arabia worked to restore its East–West pipeline, with the ten-year coming into the day at 5.01% after its first close above 5% since July 2007.

archive.headline: The hike landed. The bond market blinked first.
archive.summary: Weekend edition. The Fed's unanimous 25bp on Wednesday took the Dow down 631 points and Thursday gave most of it back, with the S&P up 1.14% to 7,637.76 as the ten-year fell to 4.93% and oil slid. The weekend risk was the Iran war, with Trump saying he was near a decision on resuming large-scale strikes.

archive.headline: The ten-year touched 5% into the decision. The hike is not the event.
archive.summary: FOMC day. The 10-year had closed at 5.00% after touching 5.04%, the highest since 2007, with a 25bp hike priced at 92–94%. WTI had jumped 5.1% to $106.56 as fighting intensified in the Middle East; every US sector but energy closed red on Tuesday.

archive.headline: Core CPI ran hot into an FOMC that is now 90% priced to hike
archive.summary: Weekend edition. Core CPI rose 0.3% on the month against 0.2% expected, PPI came in at 5.4% year-over-year, and September hike odds moved from 61% to about 90%. Equities closed the week higher regardless — S&P +0.86% Friday, VIX −11% — while the 10-year finished at 4.96%.

archive.headline: Core CPI at a four-month high, hike odds jump to ~90%
archive.summary: Headline CPI held at 3.4% year-over-year but core rose 0.3% on the month against 0.2% expected. Energy added 2.1% and gasoline 3.9%; airline fares rose 2.7%. Equities rallied regardless — S&P +0.86%, VIX −11% — while the 10-year touched 4.97%.

archive.headline: PPI beats, ECB hikes to 2.50%
archive.summary: August PPI came in at 5.4% year-over-year against 5.3% expected with July revised up from flat. The ECB raised its deposit rate 25bp to 2.50% effective 16 September and cut its 2028 inflation forecast to 2.1%. September hike odds moved from 61% to 72%.

archive.headline: Oil tops $100, Dow sheds 400 more
archive.summary: Brent broke $100 for the first time since July and the 10-year yield hit a three-year high. Amgen fell over 10% on a failed cardiovascular trial and software names sold off. Barclays nonetheless lifted its year-end S&P target to 7,950.
